q: Which Notes app task truly needs a Cloud Function?
o: Keeping a note count users cannot fake
why: A trusted count must not be written by the client. The other tasks are plain reads and writes that rules can protect.

q: You want code to run every morning at 9, even when no app is open. Which trigger fits?
why: Scheduled functions run on a timetable using Cloud Scheduler.

q: Your function needs a mail service API key. Where should the key live?
o: In Secret Manager, read with defineSecret
why: Secrets set with functions:secrets:set are stored encrypted and given only to functions that list them.

q: You must upgrade to the Blaze plan before you can run a Cloud Function in the Emulator Suite.
why: The emulator runs functions on your computer on any plan. Blaze is needed only to deploy.

q: Users say the first tap on a rarely used function is slow. What is the likely cause?
why: A function that has been idle needs a fresh copy started. minInstances can help, but you pay for idle copies.

q: Reloading the page at /notes/n1 on your hosted single-page app shows Not found. What fixes it?
why: The rewrite makes Hosting serve the app's index.html for every path so the app can handle routing.

q: Saving a photo's download URL in a private note is safe because Storage rules still protect the file.
why: A download URL carries a token; anyone with it can open the file. Store the path instead.

q: You want a teammate to test a new feature without changing the live site. What do you do?
o: Edit files on the live site
Start the emulator on their phone
why: A preview channel gives a temporary URL separate from the live site and expires on its own.
